items.title: Ship fuel shortage looms as refiners strained by war favour other products
items.summary: Higher bunker fuel costs could also in turn feed into shipping rates. Fuel oil joins gasoline, diesel and jet fuel among the refined products struggling to keep up with demand. Nigeria's 650,000-barrel-per-day Dangote refinery, for example, has ramped up diesel, gasoline and jet fuel exports, while its fuel oil exports have dropped, according to Kpler.

items.title: Kuantan cops nab daycare centre worker after video shows toddler being shaken, hair pulled
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 7 — Police have arrested a woman to assist investigations into an incident where a two-year-and-eight-month-old boy was allegedly mistreated at a child daycare centre in Bukit Setongkol here. Kuantan police chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said the department received a report about a viral video of the incident on social media at 10.34am yesterday. He said preliminary investigations indicate the incident occurred on Aug 11.

items.title: Hadi’s 2014 US ‘topple govt’ claim sparks three police reports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Three police reports were lodged yesterday over a claim by PAS president and Marang Member of Parliament Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang that the United States had offered assistance to topple the Malaysian government in 2014. The reports were lodged by Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Bandar Tun Razak branch vice-chief V. Jonathan, PKR Bandar Tun Razak branch women’s chief Mazlina Osman and Bandar Tun Razak Angkatan Muda Keadilan deputy chief Amarul Hisham Jalil at the Cheras Police Station here. “Police reports have been lodged.

items.title: SUV driver arrested after allegedly running red light, fleeing crash
items.summary: MIRI: An SUV driver who allegedly ran a red light and crashed into a motorcycle at a traffic junction here on Saturday has been arrested. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the foreign suspect, in his 30s, was arrested with the Brunei-registered Toyota Prado near the Sungai Tujoh border. He said police received a report on the 8.35pm collision involving the SUV and a motorcycle ridden by a local woman in her 30s.

items.title: Samarahan records very unhealthy API reading, 40 areas unhealthy
items.summary: Meanwhile, 40 other areas nationwide registered unhealthy API levels. In Negri Sembilan, three areas registered unhealthy air quality: Nilai (166), Seremban (163), and Port Dickson (123). Meanwhile, 24 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality, while two areas registered good readings.

items.title: Challenging terrain may have delayed six missing hikers, says guide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A mountain guide involved in the search-and-rescue (SAR) operation for six missing hikers in Gua Musang believes the group may have been delayed by challenging terrain. The 34-year-old mountain guide, who requested anonymity, said the group was unlikely to be lost, but likely took longer to navigate the difficult route. The group entered the forest via Pos Dakoh, Lojing, Gua Musang, and was scheduled to emerge via Pos Kemar in Perak on Sept 3.

items.title: Two semi-detached houses, Honda Civic damaged in Port Klang fire
items.summary: KLANG: Two semi-detached houses and a car were damaged in an early morning fire at Kampung Telok Gong, Port Klang, today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at Jalan Telok Gong at 3.01am. Firefighters arrived at the scene at 3.12am and found the fire involving two semi-detached houses measuring 24ft by 50ft.

items.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher against US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Monday, buoyed by expectations of a potential United States (US) interest rate hike following stronger-than-expected US non-farm payrolls (NFP) data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the higher-than-expected NFP suggests the US Federal Reserve (Fed) is likely to raise its benchmark interest rate at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Sept 15-16. More to come © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Oil extends gains after US and Iran strike ships
items.summary: Reuters SINGAPORE: Oil prices extended gains on Monday as tit-for-tat strikes between the US and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption from the Middle East. Brent crude futures climbed 52 cents, or 0.54 per cent, to US$96.80 a barrel by 2354 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$92.14 a barrel, up 66 cents, or 0.72 per cent. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday, US Central Command said, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, near Iran's key oil export hub.

items.title: Australia moves to give users more control over social media algorithms
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australians could be given the option of opting out of powerful social media algorithms under new legislation cracking down on big tech, a minister said Monday. It would require firms like Meta to give users the option of turning off algorithms that tailor recommendations to their personal taste. Australia implemented legislation barring children from social media platforms in December, part of a world-first crackdown designed to protect children from online bullying and "predatory algorithms."

items.title: US envoys have 'more effective proposals': Ukraine
items.summary: KYIV: Washington's envoys have brought new, "more effective" proposals on ending the war with Russia to Kyiv, a senior Ukrainian presidential official told AFP Sunday. Earlier Sunday, Volodymyr Zelenskyy had said the war with Russia looked likely to continue into the winter. Zelenskyy also said Ukraine would hold talks with the US, France and Germany, but did not elaborate.

items.title: Miracle rescues lift hopes as Nepal flood search enters 12th day
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations after catastrophic floods entered a 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescues of four survivors. Rescuers found two more people alive on Saturday, joining two saved the day before in what have been described as miraculous tales of survival. Rescue workers were experiencing "multiple challenges", he said.

items.title: Nepali woman found alive 10 days after family began mourning her death
items.summary: BETRAWATI: Believing she had perished in Nepal's deadly floods, the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death. Ten days later, rescuers found her alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village, where she had survived in a narrow pocket of air amid water and mud. Shrestha was among the hundreds missing in Betrawati, an area among the hardest hit by the floods in Nepal and engulfed with white deposits compacted almost like concrete.

items.title: The case for making Malaysia one connected production economy
items.summary: IF neighbouring states increasingly function as interconnected economic regions, Malaysia must confront a larger question. Three Pillars of Economic Federalism Malaysia needs to distinguish between three related concepts. Production federalism connects economic activity.

items.title: When employees are afraid to speak, organisations stop learning
items.summary: In the cafeteria, however there is a roar of activity and discussion among employees, with some openly voicing their views on the problems facing the organisation and what management should do to address them. Everyone is strident in their views, confidently pontificating on how the lingering problems in the organisation could be resolved. One reason is the absence of psychological safety- an environment where employees feel able to speak up, ask questions, admit mistakes, challenge ideas and offer suggestions without fear of humiliation or punishment.

items.title: Continued net interest margins compression a risk to lending environment
items.summary: Declining NIM is pronounced on Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd, according to data presented by HLIB Research in the note, although the bank remains having the highest figure among the eight banks under the research firm's coverage, at 2.3 per cent. Affin Bank Bhd had the lowest NIM during the quarter, at 1.5 per cent, followed by RHB Bank Bhd at 1.8 per cent. Malayan Banking Bhd, Public Bank Bhd, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd and Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd chalked 2.1 per cent NIM during the quarter.

items.title: Syed Azman faces test of turning HHRG assets into earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HHRG Bhd's appointment of Tan Sri Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim as executive chairman puts one of Malaysia's better-known entrepreneurs at the helm of a company that needs more than just a new growth story - it needs stronger earnings. Syed Azman, the founder of Weststar Group, takes over as HHRG continues to grapple with weaker operating performance while pursuing a diversification strategy beyond its traditional biomass and fibre businesses. That leaves Syed Azman with a fairly clear challenge: turn HHRG's asset base into recurring, higher-quality earnings.

items.title: Padi farmers demand answers over fertiliser supply delays [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation into delays in the supply of subsidised fertiliser to padi farmers must determine who was responsible and whether there were weaknesses in the procurement and supply process. Malaysian Padi Farmers Brotherhood Organisation chairman Abdul Rashid Yob said farmers wanted to know what had happened and who was responsible. He said farmers had repeatedly raised the fertiliser supply issue with the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry before action was eventually taken.

items.title: How much support flows into Malaysian homes: Breaking down the nation’s subsidy system
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Government assistance does not always come in the form of cash. For Malaysian households, support can come through direct aid, credits for essential goods, school assistance, cheaper public transport and subsidised fuel, among other measures. To put the numbers into perspective, consider a Malaysian household of two adults and two secondary-school children, with household income below RM2,500 a month, assuming the family members meet the relevant eligibility requirements.

items.title: Delay in fertiliser distribution to Kedah padi farmers: MACC opens probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened an investigation paper into delays in the distribution of supplementary compound fertiliser, known as Baja 3, to padi farmers in Kedah. The commission said its Kedah office received a complaint from Pertubuhan Persaudaraan Pesawah Malaysia (Pesawah) on Aug 26 and opened an investigation into the matter. Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim instructed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to investigate delays in the distribution of fertiliser to padi farmers in Kedah.

items.title: 'Truly scared': Blazes outpace firefighters in Indonesian Borneo
items.summary: They are fighting a perilous battle with limited weapons against fires blamed in part on a stronger-than-usual episode of the El Nino climate phenomenon parching Southeast Asia. Experts also blame climate change, decades of forest degradation and slash-and-burn land clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape. Sometimes we don't sleep," said Sampe Ritonga, fire chief for Sintang regency.

items.title: Indonesia shuts main airport, seven others after Anak Krakatoa eruptions
items.summary: JAKARTA: About 170,000 passengers were left stranded on Sunday as Indonesia shuttered its main international airport and seven others, cancelling hundreds of flights after Mount Anak Krakatoa spewed a plume of volcanic ash and lava from more than 150 kilometres away. Ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, prompting authorities to suspend operations, the ministry said. The suspension was extended until 8.59am Monday "due to increased eruptive activity at Mount Anak Krakatoa", the airport authority said in an Instagram post.

items.title: Iran threatens greater force if US launches more attacks
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Teheran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes. Teheran's top security chief, meanwhile, said Iran would establish a "prohibited zone" near the Strait of Hormuz in coming days. In response, the US struck three oil tankers it said were linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC).

items.title: Five dead, five injured after Amazon cargo plane overshoots Miami runway
items.summary: MIAMI: At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, crashed into vehicles and caught fire, officials said. The plane operating as Prime Air Flight 7598 caught fire as a result of the "crash," fire officials said. "A total of 60 fire apparatuses arrived, just short, just shy of 200 men and women from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, to begin the actual search and rescue and firefighting," Jadallah said.

items.title: German rocket reaches space
items.summary: OSLO: The uncrewed Spectrum rocket was the first commercial flight to reach orbit from continental Europe, where several nations have said they want a share of a growing market for space missions. And just made European history," Isar said in a post on the social media platform X. The event was a breakthrough for the European launch industry, giving the continent better access to space, Norway's Industry and Commerce Minister Cecilie Myrseth said in a statement.

items.title: Helping Malaysians invest smarter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission (SC) and Bursa Malaysia Bhd have launched the inaugural InvestSmart x Bursa Marketplace Fair 2026 to promote investor education and protect investors against scams. The two-day event brings together the SC and Bursa Malaysia's flagship investor engagement platforms for the first time. The collaboration highlights the importance of investor education and financial literacy as more Malaysians explore a wider range of investment products, digital platforms and information sources.

items.title: Jakarta-bound passengers advised to check flights
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Passengers travelling to Jakarta have been advised to check their flight status before heading to the airport, after the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was temporarily closed due to volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau. Civil aviation director-general Lukman F. Laisa said tests confirmed the presence of volcanic ash at the airport. Up to 10pm on Saturday, 33 flights at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport had been affected.

items.title: US Navy musician charms Sabah with 'Original Sabahan'
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A United States Navy musician has captured Sabahans' hearts after her rendition of popular local song Original Sabahan at the launch of the Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26) went viral. "It's one of those songs that everyone knows and can sing along to," she told the New Straits Times during the Pacific Partnership Band performance at a shopping mall here on Saturday. The Pacific Partnership Band will also perform at schools, the Gaya Street Market concert on Sept 11 and the Pacific Partnership Fair on Sept 12.

items.title: Three killed, others trapped in India building collapse
items.summary: NEW DELHI: A building collapse in the Indian capital New Delhi killed at least three people on Sunday, local media reports said, as authorities worked to rescue those trapped in the rubble. The building, housing mostly students, came crashing down about midday in the southwestern Satya Niketan area of the city, with police and disaster response personnel cautiously lifting the rubble using heavy machinery. Three people died in the accident, according to The Hindu newspaper and other local media reports, quoting unnamed fire services officials.

items.title: Cape Verde in mourning after children killed in bus crash
items.summary: PRAIA, Cape Verde: Cape Verde's government announced two days of mourning on Sunday after 25 people, mostly children and teenagers, were killed in a bus crash. Prime Minister Francisco Carvalho told public television station TCV he had ordered two days of mourning and promised further measures would be taken. Seven victims were buried early on Sunday.

items.title: NST Leader: Murder of journalists is now the norm
items.summary: A JOURNALIST who speaks truth to power and a gunman for hire are at two ends of the humanity spectrum. So were investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia and Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech who was acquitted on Sept 2 after nine years of trial by jury for involvement in the murder of Galizia. But something bothered Maltese newspapers with Fenech admitting that he financed the murder.

items.title: Oil importers learning to live with longer trade routes
items.summary: ENERGY trade routes that optimise distance and costs may no longer be suitable for the fractured and fractious modern world, especially for major importers. Ongoing tensions involving Iran are pushing major oil importers to develop alternative supply routes, which increasingly bypass the supply hubs that previously dominated global energy trade. Japan's evolving cocktail of crude oil purchases underscores the extent of the changes underway among top energy importers.

items.title: How a Nepalese principal saved 900 students by ordering an evacuation
items.summary: RAJENDRA Dawadi was inside his school near Nepal's Trishuli River with around 900 students when a colleague delivered an urgent warning. "My accountant came to the school and said, 'The flood is coming, the flood is coming'," the school principal said. Students were panicked, Dawadi said, and one girl fainted.

items.title: At KLIA, stranded travellers hope Jakarta flights resume soon after Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 6 — Passengers stranded for over 12 hours at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 following flight cancellations to Jakarta hope the situation will resolve quickly so they can resume their journeys. According to MAHB, the cancellations reported by airlines as at noon today involved flights scheduled between 6.45am and 11.55pm. — Bernama pic Meanwhile, Octavia Suci Siregar, 18, said her flight scheduled to depart at 9.55 pm today was also cancelled, leaving her waiting at a designated area in KLIA Terminal 1.

items.title: MACC arrests ex‑GM with ‘Datuk’ title and another suspect over alleged land‑sale corruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested two individuals, including a former general manager of a statutory body with the title ‘Datuk’, over alleged misappropriation, abuse of power, and corruption. A source said the suspects are believed to have abused their power in appointing a company for a project and in the sale of land owned by the statutory body. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrests and said the case is being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Six Penang-Jakarta flights cancelled after airport shutdown triggered by Anak Krakatau eruption, affecting 1,000 passengers
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — Six flights from Penang International Airport to Jakarta, Indonesia were cancelled today following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic dust from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau. “Passengers have received early announcements by airlines about their flight cancellations as soon as airport operations in Jakarta were ordered close, so there isn’t any extraordinary congestion at the airport. Flight operations at the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport have been suspended till 1.30 pm local time today (2.30 pm, Malaysia time).

items.title: At anti‑bullying event, Sabah Education Dept urges victims to stand firm, report abuse and seek help
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 6 — Students who face bullying are urged to come forward immediately and report the incidents to their teachers, parents and authorities. State Education Department deputy director (student development sector) Muddin Beting stressed that victims of abuse must stand firm on the truth and justice to prevent their peers from suffering the same fate in the future. Adding on, he said the Education Department commended MTPN Sabah for organising the anti-bullying programme, which he hoped would bring positive results throughout the state.

items.title: Gua Musang police: Six hikers feared missing after entering forest via Lojing and not emerging in Perak
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 6 — Six individuals — four family members and two mountain guides — who entered a forest area through Pos Dakoh, Lojing, Gua Musang on August 29 are feared missing after not leaving at Pos Kemar, Perak as scheduled on September 3. Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said family members of the hikers lodged a police report in Selangor today after they failed to return from their hike on the set date, adding that checks with the Forestry Department showed that the last contact with the group revealed that they were in the forest area in Perak. “For now, we are dealing with the Perak authorities to secure confirmation as based on their last contact, they were in Perak and no longer in Kelantan,” he said when contacted today, adding that the group had permits to enter the forest and engaged the services of two mountain guides.

items.title: Police confirm shooting of wanted drug suspect in Seremban housing area
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Police confirmed a local man suspected of drug-related activities was shot dead in a residential area in Garden Homes here early this afternoon. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the incident occurred at 1.50pm. “Yes, I confirm the incident,” he told reporters here today.

items.title: Don’t be deceived by RM2,500 deposit scam involving unofficial Kampung Jelutong SPK house offers, warns Jepak rep
items.summary: BINTULU, Sept 6 — The public have been warned against falling victim to unofficial offers to purchase houses in the Kampung Jelutong Village Expansion Scheme (SPK) in Jepak. Jepak assemblyman Iskandar Turkee said he had been informed about certain parties offering housing units in the area through unofficial channels, with prospective buyers reportedly being asked to pay a RM2,500 deposit. Handout photo shows one of the two housing models available at the Kampung Jelutong SPK.

items.title: Selangor ready to distribute face masks in worst‑hit haze areas, with priority for vulnerable groups, says exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — The Selangor Disaster Management Committee is ready to distribute face masks to the public and civil servants to cope with the ongoing haze situation. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the distribution would focus on areas recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Selangor, particularly targeting vulnerable groups. “The public is also advised to reduce strenuous outdoor activities and remain indoors if air quality is unhealthy, while staying updated on the latest API readings in their respective areas,” she added.

items.title: Seven UiTM students remain under treatment after heat‑related incident; outdoor endurance events called off
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — Seven Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) students are still receiving treatment and undergoing medical monitoring following a heat-related incident while taking part in an endurance event in Pahang on Friday. In a statement today, UiTM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin said the university management was paying particular attention to the health and welfare of all the affected students, who are being treated at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HOSHAS) in Temerloh and Jengka Hospital. “The five other students at Jengka Hospital are Nur Nabihah Musyidah Md Nasri (Johor branch, Segamat Campus), Nur Alia Farhana Abdul Fattah (Pahang branch, Jengka Campus), Muhamad Adam Azfar Suzaini and Muhammad Anas Shahrul Nizat from the Johor branch, as well as Izzharith Zafran Muhammad Zulkarnain from the Pahang branch,” he said.

items.title: Hunting team records nine crocodiles captured in four‑day Kuala Baram operation
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 6 — The crocodile-hunting team ‘Eric Cat’ has recorded the capture of nine reptiles throughout their four-day operation in Kuala Baram, which kicked off on September 2. Team spokesman Eric Chong Fook Shin said the last catch was made last night, which was a 14-foot (over 4 metres) crocodile. Chong said the 14-foot crocodile was the team’s largest catch during their Kuala Baram operation.

items.title: Zulkifli: Higher allocations show Madani govt commitment as Malaysia earns global Islamic recognition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Madani Government remains committed to strengthening Islamic affairs in Malaysia through increased funding and efforts that have helped the country achieve global recognition in several areas. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the increase in allocation for Islamic affairs from RM1.5 billion in 2023 to RM2.6 billion this year reflected the government’s commitment to advancing the sector. Zulkifli said the government would continue developing the Islamic affairs agenda within the framework of the law while upholding respect for diversity and differences in society The PMK programme, an initiative by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) and agencies under Religious Affairs, aims to bring government services closer to the people through information-sharing, engagement and various community services.

items.title: Don’t link salvation in the hereafter to politics, says religious affairs minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Differences in political support should not lead to a punitive or condescending attitude towards others, let alone linking salvation in the hereafter to membership of or support for any political organisation. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the determination of heaven and hell is the absolute right of Allah SWT and cannot be guaranteed by any individual, leader or political organisation. He said support for any political organisation was not a measure of attaining the pleasure of Allah SWT, as faith, piety and righteous deeds based on the Quran and Sunnah served as the primary foundations.

items.title: Sri Aman only area with very unhealthy API reading of 216 as of 4pm, with no hazardous readings nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — No area recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to the haze as of 4 pm today, although Sri Aman in Sarawak was the only area to record a very unhealthy reading of 216. The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal reported unhealthy API readings in 35 other areas nationwide, moderate readings in 27 areas and good readings in four areas. Sarawak remained the worst-hit state, with 11 areas recording unhealthy air quality, namely Samalaju (196), Samarahan (196), Kuching (191), Bintulu (190), Mukah (188), Sarikei (185), IPD Serian (182), ILP Miri (176), Sibu (174), Miri (170) and Limbang (157).

items.title: Budget 2027 to emphasise support for M40 and lower‑income groups, says Finance Minister’s aide
items.summary: LUMUT, Sept 6 — Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister. Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9. Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.

items.title: Doctors induce coma for Batu Pahat toddler wounded in stray dog attack
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 6 — A two-year-old girl is fighting for her life after being critically injured by a pack of five stray dogs outside her grandmother’s house in Kampung Tambak, Sungai Kelambu, Peserai in Batu Pahat yesterday. Darlinda said she found the front door open after taking a bath and saw the dogs attacking the girl outside the house. The girl was later transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital here because of the severity of her injuries, Darlinda said.

items.title: Anwar and old friend Al Gore reunite (virtually) to talk climate challenges, decades after ‘reformasi’
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he spoke with former US vice-president Al Gore about the global climate crisis, haze affecting Malaysia and the country’s transition towards cleaner energy. Anwar said Gore, who was in Singapore, had expressed sympathy over the haze after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian, Sarawak exceeded 500 two days ago. Anwar said they also discussed the wider effects of climate change, including the recent floods in Nepal.

items.title: Fadhlina praises Taanusiya’s Miss World showing and her commitment to education advocacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty, who finished third in the Miss World 2026 pageant, for championing education and advocacy as part of her cause. “I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya’s commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause. “Congratulations, Taanusiya.

items.title: Youth and Sports Ministry to prioritise grassroots sports development and athlete welfare in Budget 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — The Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS) has submitted an initial framework of its Budget 2027 proposals to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration, with grassroots sports development, youth participation and athletes’ welfare among the ministry’s priorities. Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the framework was prepared based on input gathered through the Madani Youth Budget Tour being conducted in six zones nationwide. “Although all the tour sessions have not been completed, KBS has obtained various views from youth organisations, sports associations as well as unorganised youths for review and assessment.

items.title: Anak Krakatau chaos strands Malaysians in Jakarta, with hotels full and next flights two days away
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Malaysians stranded in Jakarta after volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted flights are now scrambling for alternative arrangements, with some travellers facing delays of several days before they can return home. One traveller who goes by the moniker Spritzerphilips on Threads was a picture of fatigue and anxiety after being stranded at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after her flight, scheduled for today, was cancelled. About an hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight for Tuesday.

items.title: Water supply to 34,000 accounts in Machang expected to be restored tomorrow after pipe repairs
items.summary: MACHANG, Sept 6 — Water supply to about 34,000 consumer accounts in Machang, southern Kota Bharu and parts of Pasir Puteh is expected to be restored in stages from noon tomorrow following a main pipe leak in Pulai Chondong here. Kelantan Public Works, Infrastructure, Water and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Dr Izani Husin said the leak in the 1,100-millimetre glass-fibre reinforced plastic (GRP) pipe was detected on Friday, with excavation and repair works beginning on the same day. Meanwhile, AKSB head of Production Dr Mohd Hilmi P. Ramli said the company planned to replace the GRP pipe with mild steel pipes following the fourth leak since it was commissioned eight years ago.

items.title: FT mufti: ‘Religious exploitation’ more accurate term, not ‘riding on religion’, to describe misuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil. He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam. The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.

items.title: More money for Agriculture Ministry? Anwar says maybe — if the books stay clean, so farmers won’t suffer
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters. Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.

items.title: Kedah appeals for continued cloud seeding as Pedu, Muda and Ahning dam levels keep falling
items.summary: He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning. “The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today. Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.

items.title: Bukit Lagi Hindu temple row: Perlis police get two more days to detain activist as probe widens into criminal trespass
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation. Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today. Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.

items.title: Fadhlina pledges no SJKT closures as RM12.6m Sungai Bakap Tamil school project gets going after 17 years
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils. “We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.

items.title: Volcanic ash grounds 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights by Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK). Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724. “Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.

items.title: United Sikhs Malaysia head into Nepal’s worst-hit flood zone to help 98 kids whose parents are missing (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides. The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border. https://www.facebook.com/UNITEDSIKHSMALAYSIA/videos/06092026-mission-update-nepal-flood-reliefunited-sikhs-malaysias-team-a-is-curre/3827014714104717/ United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.
